articles.headline: U.S. levies new 25% tariff on Indian goods citing excess capacity
articles.title: U.S. announces new 25% tariffs on India, second-highest in the 14 countries against which action has been taken
articles.summary: The United States government announced a 25% import tariff on Indian goods on November 25, 2026, citing structural excess capacity that burdens American commerce. According to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, the rate could drop to 17% if a trade agreement is reached. The Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry stated it is examining the notice while bilateral negotiations continue.
articles.description: The order by the U.S. Trade Representative also opens the door for a lower 17% tariff if India and the U.S. sign a trade deal

articles.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secures record fourth presidential term in Brazil
articles.title: Lula wins a record fourth presidential term as Brazil defeats far-right, defies Trump and Meta
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic fourth presidential term in a runoff election on October 26, 2026, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party with 64 million votes. Declaring victory in Villavicencio, Mr. Lula pledged to regulate big tech companies and govern for all Brazilians. The result dealt a setback to U.S. President Donald Trump, who had supported Mr. Bolsonaro, according to special presidential advisor Celso Amorim.
articles.description: People went out to vote because we managed to convince them that their votes were extremely important to safeguarding democracy in the country, said Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following Donald Trump intervention
articles.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia reinstated Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang on Monday after a brief resignation prompted by reports of an affair with a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. President Donald Trump stated he convinced the board to reverse the decision. The move sparked sharp market gains and fierce political backlash, with congressional Democrats and Republicans vowing immediate investigations into the chipmaker and national security compliance.
articles.description: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.

articles.headline: Fuel tanker crash on Cairo highway causes massive fire killing thirty-one
articles.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
articles.summary: Thirty-one people died and twenty-one others suffered injuries after a fuel tanker crashed and burst into flames on a busy highway in the Warraq neighbourhood of Cairo on Wednesday evening, according to the health ministry. Officials stated the vehicle overturned following a fallen power cable. The regional public prosecutor initiated an investigation into the deadly accident.
articles.description: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

articles.headline: Fuel tanker crash on Cairo Ring Road causes deadly fire
articles.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites massive fire on highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 30 people
articles.summary: At least thirty people died and twenty-five others sustained injuries when a fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on the Ring Road encircling Cairo on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. The Egyptian Health Ministry reported that the incident occurred in the densely populated Waraq area of Giza, charring numerous vehicles and prompting an ongoing investigation by the Public Prosecutor's office.
articles.description: The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor’s office said in a statement

articles.headline: Global tech stocks decline further amid ongoing concerns over artificial intelligence investment
articles.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
articles.summary: Major technology firms experienced sharp share price drops on Wednesday, with losses affecting Nvidia, Anthropic, Amazon, and Meta. The downturn reflects persistent investor anxiety regarding the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending and recent political developments in the United States. Despite the market volatility, investment bank Goldman Sachs projects that artificial intelligence spending will surpass one trillion dollars in 2026.
articles.description: All three main US indexes were down in early trading, with the tech-dominated Nasdaq down almost 4%.

articles.headline: Gaza municipalities warn winter rains threaten displaced Palestinian shelter camps
articles.title: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
articles.summary: Gaza municipal leaders warned on Wednesday that upcoming winter storms threaten roughly one thousand displacement camps due to damaged drainage systems and missing repair supplies. The Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities stated that recent November rains already flooded about seventy thousand tents. Meanwhile, European Commission representatives urged Israel to permit waiting humanitarian aid trucks carrying tents to enter the enclave.
articles.description: About 200,000 tents need replacing, Gaza’s municipalities say, as the EU urges Israel to reopen all crossings.

articles.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse in Antalya over fossil fuel phase-out standoff
articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: United Nations climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye, concluded without consensus on November 22, 2026, after a record 48-hour overtime due to disagreements over fossil fuel language. The European Union, backed by roughly 130 nations, rejected the cover text for lacking phase-out commitments. Conversely, nations like India and Saudi Arabia supported the text, stressing the need for equitable energy transitions.
articles.description: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu calls for immediate end to corruption trial
articles.title: Netanyahu says corruption trial ‘must end’ as court suggests dropping case
articles.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demanded the immediate conclusion of his ongoing corruption trial after judges in Jerusalem expressed significant doubt regarding the bribery charges against him. During a court hearing on Wednesday, judges indicated low chances of conviction in Case 4000. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara stated she would consider the recommendations as political opponents negotiate coalition pacts.
articles.description: The judges' recommendations came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival.

articles.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
articles.summary: Judges at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that prosecutors drop bribery charges against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a Wednesday hearing. The panel summoned Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to state that conviction chances are low in the primary case. Netanyahu praised the development as his political rival Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form a new government administration.
articles.description: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.

articles.headline: Dozens killed in Egypt vehicle fire
articles.title: Dozens killed in Egypt vehicle fire
articles.description: At least 30 have been ⁠killed and ⁠15 injured when a vehicle carrying ‌petroleum products caught fire in Egypt.

articles.headline: Ukrainian laser downs Russian jet-powered drone in world first
articles.title: Ukrainian laser downs Russian jet-powered drone in world first
articles.description: Ukraine says that its Blysk laser system has intercepted a Russian jet-powered drone in combat for the first time

articles.headline: US Federal Communications Commission approves SpaceX space data centres
articles.title: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres
articles.summary: The United States Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy a constellation of one million space data centres named Starmind. Agency Chairman Brendan Carr stated the decision on Wednesday marks a historical first to support growing artificial intelligence computing demands. Rival companies have previously criticized the ambitious orbital infrastructure deployment plan.
articles.description: Elon Musk hails FCC's approval of SpaceX's Starmind project as 'a great asset to America and the world.'

articles.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive following government consultations
articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.summary: Nvidia unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, November 23, 2026, after board members received assurances from senior United States government officials that he posed no national security risk. The decision followed public backing from President Donald Trump, occurring less than two weeks after the 63-year-old co-founder resigned over an alleged spy scandal involving former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

articles.headline: D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov draw second World Chess Championship game
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Gukesh, Sindarov sign peace treaty in quick time
articles.summary: Grandmasters D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov agreed to a draw in the second game of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Wednesday. Utilizing the London System opening, the twenty-year-old competitors reached a threefold repetition after thirty moves. The result leaves the youngest World title match in history tied at one point each after two rounds.
articles.description: It is all-square in the youngest World title match in history; it is D. Gukesh 1, Javokhir Sindarov 1

articles.headline: Trump administration announces new tariffs on fourteen trading partners
articles.title: World reacts to Trump’s new tariffs as US stocks tumble
articles.summary: The United States administration announced new import tariffs targeting fourteen major trading partners, including China and the European Union, citing structural manufacturing overcapacity. The levies follow an investigation led by Trade Representative Jamieson Greer under Section 301. Following the announcement on Wednesday, US stock indices tumbled significantly while bond yields dropped across both America and Europe.
articles.description: The new levies come after an eight-month investigation launched by the United States Trade Representative.

articles.headline: Wall Street rallies sharply as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Main United States stock indexes surged on Monday, November 23, 2026, driven by a record 32.2% jump in Nvidia shares after the chipmaker reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The Nasdaq Composite climbed 6.69% to 24,131.42, fueled by widespread gains across artificial intelligence and tech stocks. Investors now await upcoming inflation data from Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report to gauge Federal Reserve monetary policy.
articles.description: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies students opting for three languages may continue
articles.title: Students who opted for three languages can continue with them, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court observed on November 25, 2026, that students currently opting for three languages may continue their choice without mandatory switching. The remarks responded to a Central Board of Secondary Education plea modifying evaluation rules. While Classes 7 through 9 have transitional relaxations, authorities debate implementation schedules and student incentives for learning additional languages.
articles.description: Class 7 students, along with Classes 8 and 9, had been granted a transitional relaxation from the CBSE Board exam in the third language when they reached Class 10

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes hit industrial facilities in Russia's Samara region
articles.title: Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region
articles.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks struck industrial facilities in Syzran and killed one person in Samara on November 25, 2026, according to local authorities. Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev reported that air defence downed 145 drones, causing power outages. Unverified social media reports indicated two oil refineries were hit, following Russian President Vladimir Putin's pledge to retaliate for previous strikes.
articles.description: Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages

articles.headline: IN-SPACe report highlights India's heavy reliance on imported satellite components
articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.summary: India's satellite manufacturing supply chain remains highly dependent on imports for critical components, according to an Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre report released on November 25, 2026. Chairman Pawan Goenka noted that electronics and specialized materials account for nearly 60% of costs. The autonomous body emphasized that addressing gaps in testing and procurement could help India become a global space exporter.
articles.description: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

articles.headline: Israeli airstrike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official and family
articles.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli military airstrike in the Beach refugee camp killed Hamas colonel Mohammad Abuelouf alongside his wife and two children on November 25, 2026, according to medics and Gaza's Interior Ministry. The military stated Abuelouf advanced attacks against Israeli forces in violation of a ceasefire. The attack followed another strike that killed internal security head Naeem Abu Nahel.
articles.description: The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a significant figure who "served as ‌a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s counterterrorism operations in the ‌Gaza ⁠Strip"

articles.headline: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI satellites
articles.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission approved a plan by Elon Musk-owned SpaceX to launch up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under the Starmind initiative, marking the first agency approval for a full satellite constellation. The decision requires at least one deployment by 2033 and full completion by 2040, though the agency deferred a request regarding graveyard orbits due to insufficient disposal details.
articles.description: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency […]

articles.headline: Trump’s tariff plan explained: Which countries could be hit and why?
articles.title: Trump’s tariff plan explained: Which countries could be hit and why?
articles.description: The Trump administration is preparing a fresh tariff offensive targeting major trading partners including China, India and the European Union. Here’s what the investigation is about and what it could mean for global trade.

articles.headline: Iraq court rules federal government can take over Kurdish borders and oil fields
articles.title: Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields
articles.summary: The Federal Supreme Court in Iraq ruled that federal forces can deploy to international borders in the Kurdish region and oversee oil fields. The decision supports Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's efforts to curb oil smuggling and centralise state authority. Kurdish authorities condemned the ruling as an assault on constitutional rights, while analysts highlighted potential challenges in implementing these measures against armed factions.
articles.description: The ruling comes a day after Kurdish authorities accused Baghdad of an 'assault' on the region's constitutional rights.

articles.headline: RBI bulletin indicates continued broad-based pressure on food prices in November
articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.summary: High-frequency data up to November 19 reveal persistent inflationary pressures on food items across India, according to a Reserve Bank of India report. Prices for cereals, pulses, and edible oils increased, while vegetable prices showed mixed trends. Officials noted that strong credit growth and robust export performance continue to support domestic economic resilience despite challenging global conditions and geopolitical risks.
articles.description: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.

articles.headline: United States prepares to announce tariffs on global trading partners
articles.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
articles.summary: The United States is preparing to introduce new import taxes affecting at least fourteen jurisdictions, including China, the European Union, and Japan. The upcoming announcement follows a Section 301 investigation launched after the Supreme Court invalidated previous trade measures implemented by President Donald Trump. While the administration argues the tariffs will protect American manufacturing, critics contend the policy risks increasing consumer prices and escalating international trade tensions.
articles.description: The new levies would hit many of America's trading partners, including India.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel kills Hamas’s Gaza security chief
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel kills Hamas’s Gaza security chief
articles.description: Israel assassinated Hamas’s internal security chief in Gaza City, killing him and six others in a strike

articles.headline: India records lowest net foreign direct investment in over five years during September
articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.summary: Net foreign direct investment into India dropped to negative 4.95 billion dollars in September 2026, marking the lowest level since at least March 2021. Reserve Bank of India data indicates the decline stemmed from a drop in gross inflows to 5.9 billion dollars alongside a surge in outward investments and profit repatriations by foreign companies totaling 10.8 billion dollars.
articles.description: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

articles.headline: Ukraine reports five Russian military jets damaged in strike on Savasleyka airfield
articles.title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
articles.summary: Kyiv's General Staff stated that three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged during a drone strike on the Savasleyka airfield located 300 kilometres east of Moscow. Russian officials have not commented on the airfield attack, which follows separate overnight strikes on oil refineries in the Samara region that left one person dead, according to regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev.
articles.description: The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine.

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza City
articles.title: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
articles.summary: An Israeli air strike in the Gaza Strip killed Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, a senior Hamas internal security official, along with three members of his family at dawn. The military described the target as a terrorist. The attack caused extensive damage in Shati refugee camp, drawing strong condemnation from the Hamas-run interior ministry amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two teenage daughters, doctors say.

articles.headline: Indian stock indices and rupee surge amid foreign capital inflows
articles.title: Stock indices gain 1.85%, rupee surges to 8-month high aided by foreign inflows, low crude prices
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices on November 25, 2026, recorded a significant gain of 1.85 percent backed by fresh large-cap buying and easing Brent crude oil prices below $90 a barrel. Simultaneously, the Indian rupee surged to an eight-month high against the dollar, reaching 92.23 in the interbank market. Analysts attributed the positive financial momentum to robust foreign portfolio investor inflows and improved domestic market liquidity.
articles.description: Investors' wealth went up by ₹3.49 lakh crore to ₹5,12,48,042.08 crore (USD 5.54 trillion) on November 25

articles.headline: Bangladesh tightens border security and deploys paramilitary forces
articles.title: Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons
articles.summary: Bangladesh deployed 108 platoons of border paramilitary forces across seven districts to maintain order amid rising political tensions and violence surrounding the planned return of exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Authorities increased surveillance and patrols following incidents of arson and clashes linked to the banned Awami League party ahead of December.
articles.description: The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions

articles.headline: Solomon Islands signs security treaty with Australia
articles.title: Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
articles.summary: The Solomon Islands and Australia signed a security treaty on Wednesday prohibiting foreign military bases on the island nation. Australia will provide 740 million Australian dollars over ten years to support infrastructure and education. The agreement requires the Solomon Islands to consult Canberra on critical infrastructure deals, marking a shift away from recent Chinese influence.
articles.description: Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.

articles.headline: Leaked Russian statistics reveal nearly 500,000 military fatalities
articles.title: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war
articles.summary: Leaked official data from Russia's statistics agency Rosstat, analysed by the BBC and independent outlet Mediazona following a cyber-attack, indicates that at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The records demonstrate severe casualties among young adults and specific military units, far exceeding figures acknowledged publicly by Moscow while aligning with open-source tracking efforts.
articles.description: Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia.

articles.headline: Russian air strikes across Ukraine kill five and damage energy infrastructure
articles.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill five, cause power outages in five regions
articles.summary: Russian military strikes across multiple Ukrainian regions killed at least five people, injured dozens, and severely damaged essential energy facilities, according to local authorities. The attacks caused widespread power outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Odesa, and Kharkiv. Furthermore, the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant temporarily lost external power following shelling, forcing it to switch to diesel generators during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: A Ukrainian official says attacks on Zaporizhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions damaged a number of energy sites.

articles.headline: Rapid Support Forces drone attacks kill nineteen people in Sudan
articles.title: Sudan’s RSF kills at least 19 in drone attacks on Blue Nile state
articles.summary: At least 19 individuals were killed and 20 others wounded after paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched overnight drone strikes targeting Damazin, the capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state. A rights group and military sources reported that the bombardment hit residential areas, electricity infrastructure, and a nearby dam. This violence forms part of the ongoing civil war between Sudanese military factions that began in April 2023.
articles.description: The attacks on Blue Nile state also wounded at least 20 people – in a drone war that is quickly escalating.

articles.headline: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
articles.title: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
articles.description: A decade after the Brexit vote, a new deal brings Britain and the EU closer, with economic gains for both sides.

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli military air attack in the Gaza Strip killed Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, the director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters. The enclave's Ministry of Interior stated that the strike targeted their residence in the Shati refugee camp. This incident occurred shortly after the killing of another senior security official amid continuing violence in the region.
articles.description: Gaza's internal security director and his family are among seven Palestinians killed by Israeli forces on Wednesday.

articles.headline: Huawei found guilty of trade secrets conspiracy and bank fraud in U.S.
articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.summary: Following a two-month trial in a Brooklyn court, a United States jury found Chinese technology firm Huawei guilty of ten out of twelve counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud. Jurors acquitted the company of an overarching racketeering charge. Defence attorney Brian Heberlig announced that Huawei plans to appeal the convictions following the sentencing scheduled for September 2027.
articles.description: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.

articles.headline: Chinese Communist Party investigates Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining
articles.title: Who is Chen Jining, China’s latest Politburo member under investigation?
articles.summary: The Chinese Communist Party launched an anticorruption probe into Shanghai secretary Chen Jining for alleged serious violations of discipline and law. Announced by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the investigation makes Chen the fourth high-ranking Political Bureau member to be ousted in two years. President Xi Jinping's ongoing purge aims to enforce strict party discipline ahead of the upcoming congress.
articles.description: Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form coalition government
articles.title: Could Netanyahu take Israel into another war with Iran to cling to power?
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is working to assemble a coalition government to avert potential political maneuvers by interim Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding Iran. Eisenkot currently lacks a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Intelligence officials and analysts dispute claims of an imminent military threat from Tehran, suggesting any new conflict could be politically motivated to delay ongoing leadership negotiations.
articles.description: As Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot moves to form a government, could war with Iran derail talks and save Netanyahu?

articles.headline: Leaked documents reveal FIFA considered 96-year private equity deal
articles.title: Leaked FIFA documents show Infantino’s 96-year private equity plan for World Cup
articles.summary: Leaked documents reviewed by The Associated Press show FIFA president Gianni Infantino planned to sell stakes in the World Cup for 96 years through a for-profit subsidiary named FIFA Forward Enterprises. The secretive project, developed with Joshua Kushner's firm Thrive Capital, collapsed following a global backlash. Infantino now faces his first presidential election challenge ahead of a March vote in Morocco.
articles.description: The leaked documents, including a FIFA in-house risk assessment, show its own finance officials “were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction”

articles.headline: Trump administration prepares new tariffs following excess industrial capacity probe
articles.title: U.S. set to slap tariffs on China, EU and others after probe on excess industrial capacity: report
articles.summary: The United States administration is set to release findings from a Section 301 investigation concerning excess industrial capacity across sixteen trading partners, with new import duties expected. According to sources, the proposed levies will stack on previous tariffs and replace measures struck down by the Supreme Court in February. The probe covers major economies including the European Union, China, and India.
articles.description: India was also named among 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners; Together, the duties are meant to ​rebuild Trump’s global “Liberation Day” tariffs that were struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February

articles.headline: Supreme Court sets aside High Court order for inquiry into Rahul Gandhi
articles.title: Supreme Court sets aside Allahabad High Court order for CBI, ED enquiries into DA complaint against Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: The Supreme Court set aside Allahabad High Court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate to probe a disproportionate assets complaint against Lok Sabha Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi. A three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant ruled that Gandhi must be impleaded as a party and heard from the threshold, criticizing the previous in-chamber proceedings.
articles.description: The top court directs the Congress leader to be impleaded as a party in the High Court case

articles.headline: Flipkart chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down
articles.title: Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down as Flipkart CEO
articles.summary: Flipkart announced that Chief Executive Officer Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down after more than eleven years with the Bengaluru-based e-commerce firm. Walmart International President Chris Nicholas credited Krishnamurthy with driving rapid expansion and scaling flagship events. Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the board will oversee operations until a successor is named in the coming weeks.
articles.description: In the interim, Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the Flipkart board will oversee operations

articles.headline: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi drones following strike on Hodeidah
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi attacks after Hodeidah strike
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia reported that its air defense systems intercepted multiple drones over Ras Tanura and the Eastern province on Wednesday morning. According to coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki, the action followed a Saudi-led coalition air strike on the rebel-held Yemeni port city of Hodeidah. The escalation comes amid rising tensions and mutual attacks targeting strategic regional infrastructure.
articles.description: The escalation comes after the Yemeni rebel group threatened to attack the kingdom's Red Sea ports in retaliation.

articles.headline: Pakistan launches its first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to space station
articles.title: From stargazing to space: Pakistan watches its first astronaut take flight
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became Pakistan's first astronaut after lifting off on a Chinese rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre on Wednesday morning. Crowds watched the historic launch live in Islamabad at the headquarters of the Pakistan Space & Upper Atmosphere Research Commission. The spacecraft successfully docked at China's Tiangong space station hours later as part of a joint mission.
articles.description: Students and stargazers packed SUPARCO's auditorium before dawn to watch Zeeshan Ali reach orbit on a Chinese rocket.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues notice to Delhi Police on bail pleas by activists
articles.title: SC issues notice to Delhi Police on pleas by Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice on November 25, 2026, regarding interim bail petitions filed by activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Both individuals have spent over six years in custody under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act while awaiting trial for the violence that erupted during protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act.
articles.description: In their pleas before the top court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry

articles.headline: Microsoft declares emergency overhaul following historic global technical outage
articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after historic outage, internal memos show
articles.summary: Microsoft Corporation declared a severe emergency alert to fix engineering vulnerabilities after a major November outage disrupted global services including Exchange Online and Teams. According to internal company memos reviewed by Reuters, executives cited fragmented diagnostic data and slow patch deployments. Leadership established five new workstreams and set a resolution target of one hour for future incidents.
articles.description: The November 12-13 outage ​hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms ⁠and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure

articles.headline: Two Indian nationals injured in Houthi militia attack in Riyadh
articles.title: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Riyadh; New Delhi condemns strike
articles.summary: Two Indian citizens and three Nepalese nationals were among eleven people injured on November 24, 2026, when Yemen's Houthi militia targeted a tower in the Saudi capital of Riyadh. Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence described the incident in the King Abdullah Financial District as a terrorist attack. The Indian embassy confirmed the injuries and stated that assistance is being provided.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia

articles.headline: Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali docks at Chinese space station
articles.title: Pakistan rejoices as country’s first astronaut enters orbit
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali docked at China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday, becoming the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign astronaut aboard the facility. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the milestone as proof of bilateral friendship. Ali will spend up to ten days on the station during the joint crewed mission aimed at expanding international research.
articles.description: Zeeshan Ali makes history as the first foreign national to board China's space station

articles.headline: Landmine casualties rise globally as the international ban faces withdrawals
articles.title: Why are landmine casualties rising as the global ban comes under threat? | Explained
articles.summary: Landmines and unexploded ordnance killed or injured more individuals in 2025 than in any year since 2020, according to the annual Landmine Monitor report released by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines. Published on November 25, 2026, the findings coincide with the Mine Ban Treaty experiencing its first-ever withdrawals since coming into force on March 1, 1999.
articles.description: Why is the Mine Ban Treaty facing a crisis? Why are more civilians falling victim to landmines? Are countries turning away from the landmine ban?

articles.headline: India warns against technology weaponisation and urges inclusive governance
articles.title: India warns against using tech for strategic one-upmanship, calls for inclusive AI governance
articles.summary: India cautioned the United Nations Security Council against using technology for strategic one-upmanship during a high-level open debate on conflict resolution. Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni emphasized that artificial intelligence must remain human-centric and called for inclusive international cooperation. United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres also voiced serious concerns regarding algorithmic targeting in modern warfare.

articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resumed his role as CEO of Nvidia, the world's most valuable semiconductor company, just 11 days after resigning amid reports of extramarital affairs and a potential Chinese spy plot. His reinstatement followed intense pressure from the Trump administration and Silicon Valley figures, despite ongoing FBI, Justice Department, and SEC investigations into the company.
articles.description: Nvidia chief's 'mistakes' had consequences far beyond Silicon Valley. He is back nonetheless, in less than two weeks.

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes kill seven in Gaza amid meningitis outbreak
articles.title: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill 7 as doctors warn of meningitis outbreak
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip killed at least seven Palestinians on Tuesday, including police officers and a child. Simultaneously, the Ministry of Health issued an epidemic alert, reporting a surge in meningitis cases to 272 in October. Health officials warn that deteriorating conditions threaten thousands of lives as the total death toll continues rising.
articles.description: Gaza health officials say meningitis cases rose to 272 in October, more than eight times the typical monthly rate.

articles.headline: Andy Taylor, original guitarist for English new wave band Duran Duran, dies
articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.summary: Andy Taylor, founding guitarist of the 1980s English new wave group Duran Duran, has died at age sixty-five. His family and bandmates confirmed the passing in a joint statement, praising his musical impact. The artist had publicly disclosed in November 2022 that he was living with stage four metastatic prostate cancer during the band's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction.
articles.description: The band’s imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as ‘Girls on Film’ and ‘Union of the Snake’ and the moody ballads ‘The Chauffeur’ and ‘Save a Prayer’

articles.headline: Donyell Malen penalty secures Roma a draw against Paris Saint-Germain
articles.title: Malen and Roma deny injury-hit PSG in Champions League draw
articles.summary: Donyell Malen converted a late penalty to earn Roma a two-all draw against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday at the Parc des Princes. The result halted the reigning champions' twelve-match winning run and their perfect record in this season's league phase. Mario Hermoso opened the scoring for Roma before Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele scored for Paris Saint-Germain.
articles.description: Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain held to 2-2 draw by Roma as injury-ravaged squad struggle.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules speedy trial right does not guarantee bail for criminals with prior convictions
articles.title: Criminal with previous conviction can't be given bail only on strength of right to speedy trial: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India set aside a January 2026 order from the Punjab and Haryana High Court that had granted bail to an accused murderer who concealed a previous conviction for attempted murder. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar delivered the November 18 ruling, emphasizing that courts must balance an accused individual's right to a speedy trial under Article 21 of the constitution against societal and victim interests.
articles.description: "The right to a speedy trial is always considered to be a facet of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, but, at the same time, when the accused is involved in committing a heinous offence, the right of the accused and the interest of the society, including the interest of the victim and his family, is also required to be seen," says bench

articles.headline: Manchester United draw two-two with Sporting Lisbon in Champions League
articles.title: Man United denied at Sporting as referee overshadows Fernandes double
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino experienced a frustrating first match in charge of Manchester United on Wednesday as his side drew two-two against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League. Bruno Fernandes scored twice against his former club, while Luis Suarez netted a brace for the hosts, aided by a decisive goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. Youri Tielemans was also sent off late in the game.
articles.description: Bruno Fernandes nets twice in Lisbon, but referee's decisions in spotlight as Mauricio Pochettino denied first win.

articles.headline: Naval apprentice arrested for allegedly spying at Mumbai dockyard
articles.title: Trainee recorded 90 videos of sensitive installations inside Naval dockyard: Mumbai Police tell court
articles.summary: Mumbai Police informed a court on Monday that a 21-year-old Naval dockyard apprentice, Bunty Ramprakash Meena, recorded approximately 90 videos of sensitive military facilities. Arrested last week, Meena allegedly communicated with suspected Pakistani intelligence operatives via Instagram and WhatsApp. Authorities are currently investigating his contacts and potential financial transactions to determine the extent of the espionage network.
articles.description: Investigators are continuing efforts to establish the identities of other participants in the alleged group calls and ascertain the extent of the suspected information-sharing network, a Mumbai Police official said

articles.headline: South Korea issues air raid alert after Russian jets approach airspace
articles.title: Why S Korea issued air raid alert after Russian jets flew near its airspace
articles.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly issued air raid warnings for Ulleung Island on Tuesday after five Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone. Although no Russian planes entered sovereign airspace, the alert caused confusion as authorities initially suspected a North Korean incursion. Seoul has lodged a formal complaint with the Russian military.
articles.description: South Korean authorities issue air raid warnings after several Russian jets were on verge of entering its airspace.

articles.headline: Google files patent for custom artificial intelligence video streaming feeds
articles.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
articles.summary: Google recently filed a patent for a system called My Channel, which aims to generate personalized entertainment using demographic data and large language models. Although the patent was rejected, the proposed technology would create tailored films featuring users as the main characters by utilizing their viewing history, location data, and contextual inputs from various connected streaming platforms.
articles.description: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come […]

articles.headline: Russian air strike kills two in Zaporizhzhia following naval drone attack
articles.title: Russian strike kills two in Ukraine, days after ship attack off Libya
articles.summary: A Russian air strike on Zaporizhzhia killed two people and wounded over 40 on Tuesday, one day after Ukraine claimed to have sunk a Russian warship in Libya. Both nations launched hundreds of drones overnight, with Poland reporting a brief Russian drone incursion into its airspace. Russia continues to target Ukrainian energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping.
articles.description: Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia destroyed a house and damaged a five-storey apartment building, Ukrainian officials said.

articles.headline: North Korea orders Swiss diplomatic representative to leave the country
articles.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row
articles.summary: North Korea ordered Switzerland's diplomatic representative to depart within forty-eight hours and closed the office following a dispute over Swiss sanctions targeting the Songdowon international children's camp. State media condemned the sanctions as a hostile act linked to allegations involving Ukrainian children. Swiss authorities stated that bilateral relations will continue through embassies in Bern and Beijing despite the diplomatic fallout.
articles.description: Swiss officials said relations would be kept through North Korea's embassy in Bern, and its own embassy in Beijing.

articles.headline: Origins and evolution of body mass index as obesity measure
articles.title: How waistlines, organ function tell a better story of obesity than BMI does
articles.summary: The body mass index originated in 1832 when Belgian astronomer Adolphe Quetelet sought to understand human populations using height and weight measurements. Originally known as the Quetelet Index, the ratio was renamed in 1972 by United States physiologist Ancel Keys after determining it best represented body fat, though it cannot distinguish between muscle mass and excess fat.
articles.description: In 2025, The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology established a commission of 58 experts from different countries to set obesity-related guidelines. A new study in Nature has tested whether the commission’s recommendations can actually distinguish between people at different levels of risk, with data from 8.4 lakh adults

articles.headline: Supreme Court signals intent to stay high court order on civic polls
articles.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
articles.summary: The Supreme Court indicated it is inclined to stay a Calcutta High Court order that deferred municipal elections in Kolkata pending a challenge on ward delimitation. Justices emphasized that pending elections should not be postponed unreasonably. The Bench asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instructions on the matter before November thirty.
articles.description: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court

articles.headline: United States Department of Education investigates Virginia school closures
articles.title: US Education Department probes Virginia schools after sexual abuse scandal
articles.summary: The United States Department of Education announced an investigation and funding freeze targeting an Albemarle County district after local authorities shut down twenty-nine schools. Secretary Linda McMahon confirmed the enforcement action following revelations that over five hundred staff members missed routine background checks, though officials emphasized none are suspected of child abuse.
articles.description: Virginia schools face scrutiny after revelations of abuse and widespread failures in mandatory staff background checks.

articles.headline: Singapore agrees to US cooperation following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
articles.title: U.S. targets chip smuggling to China after Huang's return to scandal-hit Nvidia
articles.summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced on November 24, 2026, that his nation will cooperate with the United States to prevent companies from rerouting advanced semiconductors to Southeast Asia and China. The development follows the U.S. Commerce Department adding Megaspeed International and several affiliates to its Entity List after Jensen Huang returned as chief executive officer of Nvidia following a brief resignation.
articles.description: Jensen Huang resigned over extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy

articles.headline: Voyager 1 becomes first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth
articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.summary: NASA announced that the Voyager 1 spacecraft crossed the historic milestone of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. Launched on September 2, 1977, the 49-year-old probe is currently travelling through interstellar space more than 16 billion miles away, with radio signals now taking a full 24 hours to travel between the spacecraft and mission controllers.
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

articles.headline: Bharti Airtel invests twelve billion rupees in Assam data centres
articles.title: Airtel to invest ₹1,200 cr in 3 data centers in Assam
articles.summary: Telecommunications firm Bharti Airtel announced plans to invest approximately twelve billion rupees to construct three data centres across Assam. The initiative includes a seven-billion-rupee facility in Guwahati alongside projects in Jorhat and Silchar. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma noted that the development highlights growing investor confidence and will expand digital infrastructure in the region.
articles.description: All three data centers,Guwahati, Jorhat and Silchar, are expected to be in place by 2028

articles.headline: What’s behind Europe’s protests?
articles.title: What’s behind Europe’s protests?
articles.description: Increase in protests and industrial disputes across EU and UK.

articles.headline: Malaysia plans to repatriate over six thousand Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.title: Malaysia set to return thousands of Rohingya refugees to Myanmar
articles.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Tuesday that the country will return more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar through naval vessels and aircraft beginning December 6. The initiative follows a ruling by the International Court of Justice concerning Myanmar security forces and comes as Malaysia argues that hosting over 225,000 registered refugees has created an unsustainable financial burden.
articles.description: The announcement comes five days after the ICJ ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.

articles.headline: VCK leader urges Tamil Nadu commission to enact anti-honour killing law
articles.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
articles.summary: Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram Member of Parliament Thol. Thirumavalavan submitted a memorandum to the Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, asserting that choosing a partner is a constitutional freedom. He urged the panel to recommend a comprehensive State law against honour crimes, establish a framework for mob violence accountability, and mandate official protection for couples.

articles.headline: Migrant wrongly deported by Trump leaves US for Spain
articles.title: Migrant wrongly deported by Trump leaves US for Spain
articles.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia has arrived in Spain with his wife after a 20-month legal battle with the Trump administration.

articles.headline: Elderly man with Alzheimer’s rescued after 11 days in Amazon jungle
articles.title: Elderly man with Alzheimer’s rescued after 11 days in Amazon jungle
articles.description: A 74-year-old man with Alzheimer's has been found alive after missing for 11 days in Brazil's Amazon rainforest.

articles.headline: US Army hails controlled explosion of toxic explosives in Iowa
articles.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
articles.summary: The United States military declared a controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of deteriorating lead azide in Middletown, Iowa, a massive success. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle stated that mitigation efforts exceeded expectations with no initial air readings above zero. The operation proceeded following legal challenges and public concern, drawing relief from local residents alongside calls for continued transparency.
articles.description: Despite widespread concern from residents ahead of the blast, officials say that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.

articles.headline: World Food Programme warns global trade route disruptions threaten millions with hunger
articles.title: Wars choke global food routes, threatening aid for 7.3 million, WFP warns
articles.summary: World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg warned the United Nations Security Council on Monday that disruptions across the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandeb, and the Black Sea could increase operational costs by $727 million by mid-2027. Lindberg stated that these chokepoints threaten food assistance for 7.3 million people worldwide amid rising conflicts and climate shocks affecting global grain and fertilizer supplies.
articles.description: WFP Executive Director Luke Lindberg decries ‘political problem’ as grain is 'not reaching the people who need it'.

articles.headline: US Army destroys volatile lead azide explosives during Iowa military operation
articles.title: US Army declares Iowa lead azide detonation ‘tremendously successful’
articles.summary: United States Army officials confirmed the successful destruction of approximately 4,500 kilograms of deteriorating lead azide at an Iowa military base after a controlled detonation. Major General Eric Shirley stated the mission exceeded expectations with zero infrastructure damage. While Environmental Protection Agency sensors initially detected no airborne lead, independent experts emphasised the ongoing need to monitor potential environmental breakdown products and toxic risks.
articles.description: Army hails Iowa's lead azide disposal operation as some experts warn of potentially hidden toxins.

articles.headline: Donald Trump details efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
articles.title: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump confirmed his direct involvement in convincing corporate directors to restore Jensen Huang to his leadership position at Nvidia. Officials indicated the administration prioritised maintaining technological dominance in artificial intelligence and preventing foreign recruitment. Mr. Huang resumed his duties following a brief resignation sparked by personal conduct inquiries involving executive relationships.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, following his recent ouster

articles.headline: Overthrown leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh on December 16
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16
articles.summary: The ousted former prime minister intends to travel back from Indian exile to Dhaka on December 16, according to her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's press secretary stated that the government expects her extradition as a convicted fugitive following her death sentence by the International Crimes Tribunal for orchestrating a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising.
articles.description: Hasina urges Dhaka to arrange her return on the national airline, as government says she can only be extradited.

articles.headline: Bangladesh government vows to arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina
articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam stated that Bangladesh will arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina upon her planned return in December 2026. Dhaka is currently seeking her extradition from India under an existing treaty. Ms Hasina faces a death sentence following a 2024 uprising, prompting renewed street protests and clashes across multiple districts by supporters of her banned Awami League political party.
articles.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

articles.headline: D. Gukesh faces Javokhir Sindarov in World chess championship
articles.title: World chess championship: Gukesh to open title defence with black
articles.summary: Defending champion D. Gukesh will play with black pieces in the opening game of the World chess championship against challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. The best-of-fourteen match begins on Tuesday, following a colour draw at the opening ceremony. Gukesh acknowledged his rival's strong form and consistency, noting that the upcoming encounter will present a genuine test for his title defence.
articles.description: The first game of the best-of-14 match against Sindarov will be played on Tuesday

articles.headline: Six people killed in plane crash off the Mississippi coast
articles.title: Two children among six dead after plane crash off Mississippi coast
articles.summary: Six individuals, including two children aged eight and ten, died after a Cessna 210 aircraft crashed into the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Mississippi on Tuesday. According to the United States Coast Guard, divers recovered the bodies from the fuselage after air traffic control lost contact with the flight traveling from New Orleans to Fort Myers.
articles.description: Divers found the bodies of three adult, one teenager aged 16, and two boys, aged 12 and 10, in the wreckage.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia highlights US-China technology rivalry
articles.title: What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump
articles.summary: The billionaire executive's reinstatement as chief executive officer has drawn intense international scrutiny and sparked debate in Washington and Beijing regarding semiconductor export restrictions. Chinese President Xi Jinping is reportedly monitoring the situation closely as trade negotiations approach, while the United States Bureau of Industry and Security continues tightening rules on advanced computing access.
articles.description: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition launches renewed military strikes on Hodeidah port in Yemen
articles.title: Could renewed strikes on Hodeidah port worsen Yemen’s humanitarian crisis?
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition conducted new attacks against Houthi targets at Yemen's vital Hodeidah port on Wednesday. The escalation responds to recent Houthi territorial gains and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia. Handing critical commercial imports and humanitarian aid, the port has faced extensive damage from a decade of conflict and previous foreign military interventions.
articles.description: Disruptions at Yemen's largest seaport could exacerbate hardships for millions of Yemenis, aid experts warn.

articles.headline: British military relocates aircraft to hangars to guard against drone attacks
articles.title: UK military ‘moving aircraft to hangars in case of drone attacks’
articles.summary: Britain's Ministry of Defence is reportedly moving Royal Air Force planes into hangars and hardened shelters overnight alongside installing anti-drone nets. Security precautions follow warnings regarding potential sabotage and drone threats from foreign actors. The ministry noted it constantly adapts to counter emerging risks while investing heavily to strengthen infrastructure protection across critical military sites.
articles.description: Experts say the move is a 'logical response' if there is intelligence suggesting a likely drone threat.

articles.headline: Defending champion Gukesh faces challenger Sindarov in Geneva World Chess Championship
articles.title: Defending champion Gukesh starts as an underdog in World Chess Championships
articles.summary: Reigning world champion D. Gukesh from India is set to defend his title against Uzbekistan competitor Javokhir Sindarov in a best-of-fourteen match starting Tuesday in Geneva. Gukesh enters the contest as the lowest-ranked reigning champion since official Elo ratings began in 1971, following a ratings slump, while Sindarov arrives at a career-high ranking after winning the Candidates tournament.
articles.description: India’s world beater meets a fellow 20-year old challenger who is in his peak form

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir police target locals operating from Pakistan-administered territory
articles.title: J&K Police, after killing last local LeT recruit, shift focus on locals operating from PoK; properties of seven attached
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police attached properties belonging to seven individuals based in Pakistan-administered regions following the elimination of the final local Lashkar-e-Taiba recruit. Directed by police chief Nalin Prabhat under anti-terror legislation, authorities seized land linked to suspects who allegedly crossed the border during the nineteen nineties to support militant activities within the region.
articles.description: The police suspect that the accused crossed the Line of Control into Pakistan in the 1990s for arms and ammunition training and subsequently remained associated with efforts to revive terrorist activities in the region

articles.headline: Australia proposes multibillion-dollar fines for tech giants over online harm
articles.title: Australia warns tech giants of multibillion-dollar fines for online ‘harm’
articles.summary: Major technology platforms like Google and Meta face potential financial penalties of up to five percent of their worldwide revenue under legislation detailed by Communications Minister Anika Wells. The proposed digital duty of care law allows individuals to sue platforms for enabling wrongdoing, targeting serious harms including child sexual abuse material and terrorism promotion.
articles.description: New internet safety bill expected to pass this week could impose fines of up to 5 percent of firms' global revenue.

articles.headline: Surgeons remove large pancreatic stones through keyhole procedure
articles.title: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
articles.summary: Surgeons at GEM Hospital removed large pancreatic stones measuring up to three centimeters from a forty-one-year-old male patient using laparoscopic surgery. Led by P. Senthilnathan, the medical team extracted the calculi without abdominal scars or stitches, providing relief to the patient who suffered from acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis and secondary diabetes.

articles.headline: Vehicle fire on Cairo ring road leaves thirty people dead and twenty-five injured
articles.title: At least 30 killed in Egypt vehicle fire, health ministry says
articles.summary: At least thirty people died and twenty-five others sustained injuries when a petroleum truck overturned and caught fire above a tunnel in Giza's Imbaba district on Wednesday. Egypt's public prosecutor launched an official investigation into the crash, ordering DNA collection from victims. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly directed the state to cover all medical expenses for the injured.
articles.description: An additional 15 were injured in blaze after vehicle carrying petroleum products flipped on a major road.

articles.headline: Women commission urges special investigation into illegal egg racket
articles.title: Women’s Commission urges Telangana Governor to recommend special investigation into illegal oocyte racket
articles.summary: The Telangana State Women’s Commission urged Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend a special investigation into an illegal oocyte collection racket busted in Hyderabad. Chairperson Nerella Sharada briefed the Governor on the exploitation of vulnerable women brought from multiple states, highlighting legal loopholes in the Assisted Reproductive Technology Act.

articles.headline: Nvidia board and CEO face ongoing legal risks despite presidential backing
articles.title: Nvidia and board still face legal risks after Jensen Huang's return
articles.summary: State investigations in California and Missouri are proceeding into corporate governance and potential misleading statements following executive Jensen Huang's brief resignation. Although United States President Donald Trump asserted that the reinstated chief executive officer poses no national security threat, independent shareholder lawsuits and regulatory scrutiny regarding export controls remain active.
articles.description: Nvidia’s board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, pressured by U.S. authorities, sparked a rapid stock rally but left the company facing multiple investigations, including an SEC probe and a shareholder lawsuit over governance

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu officials association seeks fair inquiry into harassment complaint
articles.title: ‘Ensure fair inquiry into complaint by IAS officer’
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu Indian Administrative Service Officers Association submitted a representation to Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar requesting a fair inquiry into a sexual harassment complaint involving a woman officer. Police registered a first information report against Kallakurichi Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam Member of Legislative Assembly C. Arul Vignesh, while an internal complaints committee was formed.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu opposes Cauvery water release decision at CWMA meeting
articles.title: T.N. opposes ad hoc release of only 2,000 cusecs at Biligundlu
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government registered its dissent at the 62nd meeting of the Cauvery Water Management Authority in New Delhi on Wednesday. Officials opposed a Cauvery Water Regulation Committee decision directing Karnataka to release only two thousand cusecs at Biligundlu for sixteen days, arguing that deficit years require pro-rata reductions based on yield assessment standards.

articles.headline: Colombian security forces storm Cartagena supermarket to rescue hostages
articles.title: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours
articles.summary: Colombian security forces freed approximately 20 shoppers and employees held hostage for 17 hours at a supermarket in Cartagena. Gunmen stormed the building on Tuesday following a failed robbery of an armoured car. President Abelardo de la Espriella authorized special forces to launch a rescue operation using stun grenades, resulting in the death of one gunman and the safe release of the remaining captives.
articles.description: One gunman was killed after what the country's president described as a robbery of a cash-laden armoured car gone wrong.

articles.headline: FIFA confirms United States and United Kingdom as 2031 and 2035 tournament hosts
articles.title: USA joint bid and UK confirmed as 2031 and 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup hosts
articles.summary: Governing body president Gianni Infantino announced that a joint North American bid led by the United States will organise the expanded 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031. Additionally, the United Kingdom will host the subsequent tournament in 2035 following an official rubber-stamping at a virtual gathering of member associations on November 23, 2026.
articles.description: The USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time

articles.headline: Election Commission directs states to correct electoral roll errors using Form 8
articles.title: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India directed chief electoral officers across twenty-five states and union territories on November 25, 2026, to rectify erroneous voter entries identified during the Special Summary Revision. Booth Level Officers will visit electors to verify demographic details and obtain Form 8 applications, ensuring no modifications occur through automated matching procedures.
articles.description: The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina plans return on 16 December
articles.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
articles.summary: Bangladesh former prime minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return home on 16 December, seeking air transport from Delhi to Dhaka. Living in exile in India since August 2024, she faces a death sentence in absentia for crimes against humanity. Bangladesh state minister Humayun Kabir dismissed her return terms. The announcement coincides with ongoing unrest linked to her banned Awami League party.
articles.description: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.

articles.headline: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi announces selected applicants for Kashi Tamil Sangamam
articles.title: 1,400 of 46,080 applicants selected to attend Kashi Tamil Sangamam: Education Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister of Education Pralhad Joshi announced on Tuesday that fourteen hundred applicants out of forty-six thousand eighty were selected for the fifth Kashi Tamil Sangamam running from November 28 to December 12, 2026. Participants will travel to Varanasi in seven groups. The edition introduces a nationwide student programme studying the Thirukkural literary work by poet Thiruvalluvar.
articles.description: The fifth edition of the Kashi Tamil Sangamam features the launch of a nationwide student engagement programme focused on learning the Thirukkural

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court defers final hearing on Great Nicobar Island project petitions
articles.title: Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court postponed its final hearing regarding forest rights violations for the Great Nicobar Island project on Wednesday after the Centre requested additional time to submit new affidavits. Presided over by Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, the bench rescheduled proceedings for January 2027 to address ongoing legal disputes over tribal rights and administrative compliance.
articles.description: Centre argues that the FRA is not implemented in the A&NI, objects to some petitions claiming that they should be heard by the NGT or SC; next hearing posted for January 13, 2027; court to hear Attorney General of India on January 22

articles.headline: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu pledges security improvements at Maiduguri rally
articles.title: Nigeria’s Tinubu pledges to bring peace to rebellion-hit border region
articles.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu promised supporters in Maiduguri on Wednesday that security forces would restore peace to the rebellion-hit border region ahead of the January 16 presidential election. Facing criticism over ongoing terrorism and kidnapping, Tinubu urged rebel fighters to surrender while security analysts noted improved accessibility across Borno State local governments.
articles.description: Tinubu is under pressure to convince voters that military operations in the country's northeast will deliver security.

articles.headline: Congress leader criticises Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing disputes
articles.title: SP, Congress seat-sharing talks turn bumpy in U.P., as Akhilesh declares candidates for five seats
articles.summary: Congress Uttar Pradesh Working Committee chief Imran Masood criticised the Samajwadi Party on Wednesday after candidates were announced for five seats while seat-sharing talks for the upcoming Assembly polls were ongoing. Masood stated that the party is not begging and will consult leadership on whether to continue discussions following the inconclusive meeting at Pramod Tiwari's Delhi residence.
articles.description: Congress leaders slammed the decision to make a unilateral announcement while talks are still underway; reject SP’s initial 26-seat proposal; SP leaders say Congress must set aside ego, understand realities

articles.headline: Kremlin rejects former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson's Western troop proposal
articles.title: Kremlin rejects ex-U.K. PM Johnson's call for a token Western force in Ukraine as unacceptable
articles.summary: The Kremlin rejected former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson's proposal to deploy a token Western military force to Ukraine, calling any foreign contingent unacceptable on Wednesday. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov criticized the suggestion following Johnson's remarks to Sky News advocating for logistical support from a coalition of willing nations.
articles.description: Russian officials have repeatedly warned that any Western troops ​deployed to Ukraine would be legitimate targets for Russian forces

articles.headline: SC to hear on November 25 pleas of Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
articles.title: SC to hear on November 25 pleas of Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
articles.description: In their pleas before the Supreme Court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry

articles.headline: Meta officials meet Congress leaders following content moderation bias allegations
articles.title: Meta officials meet Congress leaders amid allegations of bias in content moderation
articles.summary: Representatives from the technology firm Meta met with Indian Youth Congress functionaries in Delhi on November 24, 2026, following protests over alleged political content restrictions. According to Congress sources, Meta defended its synthetic content policies while denying political bias, and the disputed Instagram accounts were later restored.
articles.description: Meta was represented by Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, while Congress leader Supriya Shrinate attended the meeting

articles.headline: India separates Sheikh Hasina return plans from extradition requests
articles.title: MEA separates Sheikh Hasina’s plans to return to Bangladesh from issue of extradition
articles.summary: The Indian Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 25, 2026, that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina returning home voluntarily using a travel document is separate from Bangladesh's formal extradition request. Official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also expressed deep concern regarding ongoing violence against minorities in Bangladesh during the press briefing.
articles.description: ‘The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,’ MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said

articles.headline: Oil tankers strike naval mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says ships hit mines in Hormuz, warns vessels to coordinate passage
articles.summary: Two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on November 25, 2026, after attempting to transit an unauthorized route. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy reported the incident while the Iranian military announced enhanced surveillance systems, as Tehran maintains it will not restore normal shipping until United States demands are met.
