articles.headline: India food inflation rises to 8.94 percent in October amid supply and weather challenges
articles.title: The rising cost of putting food on the table in India
articles.summary: India's retail inflation climbed to 6.09% in October while food inflation surged to 8.94%, driven by weather disruptions, supply shortages, and rising input costs. According to experts, rural areas experienced higher pressure, and the cost of a home-cooked vegetarian thali rose significantly. Despite government cushions like cereal stocks and a free-food programme covering nearly 800 million people, economists warn of potential wage-price spirals.
articles.description: India's food inflation is broadening, squeezing household budgets.

articles.headline: Democrats secure largest House majority since 1992 following North Carolina victory
articles.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
articles.summary: The Democratic Party achieved its biggest House majority since 1992 after Chuck Hubbard defeated incumbent Republican Representative Virginia Foxx by 330 votes in North Carolina. The race was officially called on November 23, 2026, following a recount requested by Foxx. Hubbard campaigned heavily on local economic issues and the rising cost of living associated with the ongoing conflict involving Iran.
articles.description: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.

articles.headline: Climate summit ends in Antalya without final cover agreement
articles.title: COP31 ends without a deal: Is global climate diplomacy breaking? | The Hindu Analysis
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit held in Antalya, Türkiye, concluded without reaching an agreement on a final cover text. The deadlock stemmed from sharp disagreements among participating nations regarding fossil fuels, climate finance, and emissions reductions, raising questions about the future direction of international climate diplomacy and the Paris Agreement.
articles.description: In this interview, we break down the key outcomes, fault lines, fossil fuel battles, adaptation finance, and implications for developing countries, including India

articles.headline: Supreme Court criticizes Bihar judge for convicting police superintendent
articles.title: ‘Stop acting like Baahubali,’ says Supreme Court to Bihar judicial officer for FIR against Superintendent of Police
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 23, 2026, criticized a Bihar judicial officer for convicting a Superintendent of Police over an unexecuted order to register a first information report. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned Judge Anil Kumar's legal understanding, ordered him to undergo training, and stayed his prior actions.
articles.description: A Bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana questioned Bihar Judge Anil Kumar’s conduct and said his understanding of law is appalling

articles.headline: Gunmen hold dozens hostage in Colombia supermarket
articles.title: Gunmen hold dozens hostage in Colombia supermarket
articles.description: A group of armed men is holding around 20 people hostage in Cartagena, Colombia.

articles.headline: Global powers compete for mineral wealth across the African continent
articles.title: How the US, China and Russia are competing for Africa’s mineral wealth
articles.summary: The United States, China, and Russia are competing fiercely for Africa's critical mineral wealth, including cobalt in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and lithium in Mali. While Beijing dominates supply chains through investments and the Belt and Road Initiative, Washington and Moscow are deploying diplomatic, economic, and security partnerships to secure strategic resources.
articles.description: The US, China and Russia are vying for Africa’s mineral wealth, raising questions about who stands to benefit.

articles.headline: Alaska ends agreement granting Justice Department access to voter rolls
articles.title: Alaska ends deal to give voter records to US Justice Department
articles.summary: Outgoing Lieutenant Governor Nancy Dahlstrom announced that Alaska terminated a memorandum of understanding with the United States Department of Justice, ending federal access to state voter rolls. Dahlstrom stated the 2025 agreement no longer served a purpose following the midterm elections. State officials confirmed no voters were flagged or removed under the deal.
articles.description: The decision follows the conclusion of the 2026 midterm elections and an effort under Trump to gather state voter rolls.

articles.headline: Iran threatens response to any attack amid naval blockade
articles.title: Iran threatens response to any attack amid naval blockade
articles.description: Iran threatens response to any attack amid naval blockade

articles.headline: Search continues for dozens missing after Indonesia candy factory fire
articles.title: Search continues for dozens missing after Indonesia candy factory fire
articles.description: Rescuers are searching for around 30 missing workers after a candy factory fire killed at least 24 people in Banten.

articles.headline: Indian equity markets plunge heavily driven by banking sector losses
articles.title: Markets take heavy drubbing dragged by banks; Sensex plunges 1,484 points, Nifty dives to 25,349.65
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices closed sharply lower on November 23, 2026, as investors booked profits after a recent rally. The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 1,483.72 points to settle at 82,435.99, while the NSE Nifty slid below 25,350. Heavy selling pressure across banking, financial services, and metal stocks dragged the indices down significantly from earlier highs.
articles.description: Tata Consultancy Services, Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech, Titan, ITC and Infosys were among the winners

articles.headline: Rebel group halts advance and withdraws from seized areas in DR Congo
articles.title: Rebel group retreats in DR Congo after heavy clashes with government forces
articles.summary: The Convention for the Popular Revolution halted its advance toward Bunia and withdrew from recently seized territories in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Led by Thomas Lubanga, the rebel group cited a commitment made during talks hosted in Uganda by President Yoweri Museveni with the Congolese government to end the recent fighting.
articles.description: CRP halts advance towards Bunia, citing commitments made during Ugandan-mediated talks with government.

articles.headline: Ukraine reports drone strikes on Russian vessels near Libya
articles.title: Ukraine shares video of strikes on Russian ships off Libya
articles.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky released footage on Sunday appearing to show Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian ships off the Libyan coast. The attack reportedly sank a warship and damaged a cargo vessel allegedly transporting weapons. While the Kremlin warned of regional escalation, it did not directly address the incident, and local health officials confirmed receiving injured personnel.
articles.description: President Zelensky said a Russia warship was sunk, with a Russian cargo ship also hit.

articles.headline: UN climate talks collapse in Turkiye over fossil fuel disagreements
articles.title: COP31: What next after UN climate talks collapse
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya concluded in failure after participating nations deadlocked over phasing out fossil fuels and financing energy transitions for developing countries. The conference collapsed on Sunday as the European Union and vulnerable nations rejected a draft agreement supported by oil-producing states. Delegates and experts warned that the stalemate highlights persistent divisions and raises questions regarding the consensus-based negotiation process under the United Nations.
articles.description: UN member states fail to agree on how to fast-track action to reverse global warming in a blow to climate agenda.

articles.headline: Ukraine claims responsibility for naval drone attacks on Russian vessels
articles.title: Ukraine claims drone strikes on Russian ships off Libya: What do we know?
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury and struck the cargo vessel MV Angara off the coast of Libya. The operation forms part of an ongoing military campaign targeting Moscow naval assets and cargo ships linked to shadow fleets. Meanwhile, the United Nations Support Mission in Libya expressed serious concern over the incident and called for an immediate independent investigation into the attacks.
articles.description: Drone strikes on two Russian vessels near Libyan coast fuels fears of Ukraine war's spread.

articles.headline: US congressional panel urges dialogue with India on Dalai Lama succession
articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.summary: A bipartisan United States congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level diplomatic and intelligence channel with India to plan for the 14th Dalai Lama's succession. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission warned that China might turn the reincarnation process into an international legitimacy contest, while urging the recognition of the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole authority.
articles.description: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot secures first coalition agreement to form Israeli government
articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form government
articles.summary: Israel's Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman on November 24, 2026, marking the first alliance since the October 27 election. President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government by December 6 after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost his majority. Eisenkot's center-right bloc holds 48 seats, while Netanyahu's Likud retains 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset amid ongoing unity talks.
articles.description: Yashar ​said that Mr. Eisenkot had met with Avigdor ⁠Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, and they agreed on a deal afterward

articles.headline: India and China hold second round of military talks in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why the second round of Corps Commander-level dialogue in Arunachal Pradesh matters
articles.summary: India and China held nearly ten days of Corps Commander-level discussions in Arunachal Pradesh beginning on November 8, 2026, aimed at preventing border tensions along the Line of Actual Control. Lieutenant General Girish Kalia led the Indian delegation alongside a Ministry of External Affairs official during the talks, which focused on addressing competing territorial claims and ongoing military challenges in the Eastern Sector.
articles.description: The second round is aimed at establishing clearer engagement protocols between the two armies, preventing face-offs between patrol parties from escalating into larger confrontations and ensuring that communication channels remain open

articles.headline: Arsenal draw 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund in Champions League clash
articles.title: Arsenal and Dortmund draw 1-1 as Gyokeres goes from hero to villain
articles.summary: Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres scored an opening goal and missed a late header during a one-all draw against Borussia Dortmund in Tuesday's Champions League match at London's Emirates Stadium. Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund in the fifty-fifth minute. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta expressed regret over his squad's profligate attack and error-prone defensive performance.
articles.description: Arsenal dominate the chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back for a 1-1 draw in football's Champions League.

articles.headline: Real Madrid rout PSV 5-1 in Champions League match
articles.title: Bellingham stunner, Mbappe brace help Real Madrid rout PSV
articles.summary: Real Madrid defeated PSV five to one in a Tuesday Champions League fixture after falling behind to an early penalty from Ivan Perisic. Manager Jose Mourinho introduced substitute Jude Bellingham at half-time to inspire a dominant second-half comeback. Federico Valverde, Vinicius Junior, and Kylian Mbappe also scored for the Spanish club at the Santiago Bernabeu.
articles.description: Real Madrid come from behind to power past PSV Eindhoven with a 5-1 win in football's Champions League.

articles.headline: Malaysia plans to repatriate thousands of Myanmar nationals next month
articles.title: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
articles.summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Malaysia will repatriate 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, defending ongoing engagement with Myanmar leadership despite a recent International Court of Justice genocide ruling. Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees and previously sent back 10,476 individuals this year. Officials stated all upcoming returns will be covered entirely by Myanmar.
articles.description: Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ’s ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar’s leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees

articles.headline: Grameen Bank branches targeted in Bangladesh amid political unrest
articles.title: Why is Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank under attack?
articles.summary: Grameen Bank recorded 97 attacks on its branches and offices between November 10 and 23, according to internal memorandums. Managing director Sarder Akhter Hamed confirmed that attackers looted documents and destroyed records. Government officials and researchers attribute the violence to supporters of the ousted Awami League directing anger at founder Muhammad Yunus following the removal of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from power in August 2024.
articles.description: Leading financial institution has found itself at centre of tensions amid violence by Sheikh Hasina supporters.

articles.headline: Palestinian landowners face severe access restrictions in West Bank military zones.
articles.title: Occupied West Bank ‘military zones’ become de facto Israeli settler land
articles.summary: Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank face severe restrictions in accessing their ancestral lands after military zones and farm outposts effectively block their entry. Property owners report widespread destruction, theft and violence by Israeli settlers. Legal experts and human rights organisations note that such closures increasingly hand over territory to settlers despite official legal protections for local farmers.
articles.description: Closed military zones in the occupied West Bank are being seized by settlers as staging posts for pogroms.

articles.headline: India announces development package worth over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal
articles.title: India announces development package over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal’s development
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a development package of ₹15,000 crore on November 23, 2026, during talks with Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah in New Delhi. The leaders virtually launched multiple projects and a cross-border rail link. According to PM Modi, the funds aim to support Nepal's reconstruction and long-term prosperity following recent devastating floods, reinforcing bilateral ties.
articles.description: "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," says Nepal’s PM

articles.headline: Todd Blanche declines to confirm Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang investigation
articles.title: Todd Blanche declines to confirm if Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was investigated
articles.summary: United States Attorney General Todd Blanche avoided discussing whether technology executive Jensen Huang faced a federal investigation during a Washington, DC press conference. Huang resigned from Nvidia on November twelve following reports of an extramarital affair with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence, but US President Donald Trump successfully petitioned for his reinstatement.
articles.description: The US attorney general refused to discuss claims by Donald Trump that his administration conducted a 'thorough' probe.

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi details challenges regarding political alliance with the DMK
articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s agonising moments over an alliance with the DMK
articles.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi recounts her initial hesitation about forming an alliance with the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam in her memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love. She explains that the assassination of her husband, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam weighed heavily on her before political necessity ultimately prevailed.
articles.description: The alliance ahead of the 2004 parliamentary elections was born out of political necessity, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi explains in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love

articles.headline: Christian Medical College in Vellore inaugurates human metabolic chamber facility
articles.title: Human Metabolic Chamber inaugurated at CMC in Vellore
articles.summary: A state-of-the-art Human Metabolic Chamber was inaugurated at Christian Medical College in Vellore to advance research on nutrition, diabetes, obesity, and metabolic health. The facility is a collaboration between the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the medical college. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Secretary of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, officially opened the facility.
articles.description: The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer

articles.headline: Russian strikes kill at least fifteen people across Ukraine's Kyiv region.
articles.title: At least 15 killed in Ukraine’s Kyiv region as Russia intensifies attacks
articles.summary: At least fifteen people died in Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine's Kyiv region, including eleven fatalities from a building collapse in Dymer. Emergency services worked to rescue survivors and search for missing residents while energy infrastructure was targeted. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone attacks hit oil facilities inside Russia and Ukrainian forces sank a Russian corvette near Libya.
articles.description: Mulitple strikes unleashed days after Putin promises a ‘painful’ response to Ukrainian attacks.

articles.headline: Gaza turned into ‘toxic wasteland’ by Israel’s war, says new report
articles.title: Gaza turned into ‘toxic wasteland’ by Israel’s war, says new report
articles.description: Gaza turned into ‘toxic wasteland’ by Israel’s war, says new report

articles.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine behind attacks on Russian ships near Libya
articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine behind attacks on Russian ships near Libya
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has claimed responsibility for an attack that sank the Russian ship ‘Merkury’.

articles.headline: Oxfam report blames Israel for toxic pollution across majority of Gaza.
articles.title: ‘Environmental crimes’: Israel blamed for toxic pollution in 99% of Gaza
articles.summary: A report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory states that Israeli military operations have contaminated over ninety-nine percent of Gaza, creating a toxic wasteland with severe risks to human life. The bombardment generated millions of tonnes of rubble, destroyed water and sanitation plants, and released massive greenhouse gas emissions. The enclave's population faces poisoned water, unsafe soil, and acute shortages of basic supplies.
articles.description: A new report by UK-based charity Oxfam shows how Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland'.

articles.headline: Delhi court denies bail to paying guest operator over deadly building collapse
articles.title: Court rejects PG operator’s bail in Satya Niketan building collapse case, says he put profits above students’ lives
articles.summary: A Delhi court dismissed the bail application of paying guest operator Shubham Tyagi on November 23, 2026, in connection with a September 6 building collapse that caused seven deaths. Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana stated that the accused prioritized financial gain over human safety during illegal construction. Tyagi surrendered on September 11, and police have already filed a chargesheet naming six individuals involved in the tragic incident.
articles.description: ‘The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,’ the court said

articles.headline: Armed men hold hostages at Cartagena supermarket in Colombia
articles.title: Ten hostages released in standoff with gunmen at Colombia supermarket
articles.summary: Approximately twenty-five individuals remain held hostage inside an Exito supermarket in Cartagena after armed men fled an unsuccessful armoured vehicle robbery. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella confirmed that security forces and special units deployed to the La Castellana neighbourhood. Five older women were released from captivity following the initial police response.
articles.description: 10 of about 25 people held hostage were released from supermarket surrounded by police and troops.

articles.headline: Website selling lifetime press cards raises verification concerns in Delhi
articles.title: Website selling ‘lifetime press cards’ for ₹1,799 raises concerns; Delhi Police, journalist bodies flag verification challenge
articles.summary: Media representatives and the Delhi Police have raised concerns regarding the Indian Press Union, a platform selling digital and physical press identity cards for up to 1,799 rupees. According to Delhi Police IFSO Chief Sanjay Bhatia, individuals carrying cards from the platform were identified participating in October protests. Senior journalists, including Editors Guild of India member R Srinivasan and Press Club of India president Sangeeta Barooah Pisharoty, cautioned that private identity cards are not government accreditation.
articles.description: Indian Press Union offers paid identity cards to journalists, freelancers and social media content creators, promising approval within 24 hours; IFSO official says police encountered people carrying its cards, while press bodies question the organisation’s credentials and registration

articles.headline: Prime Minister Andy Burnham defends landmark EU agreement in Parliament
articles.title: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell Parliament on Monday that a new agreement with the European Union provides a realistic opportunity to improve the British economy over the next decade. The deal addresses food exports and emissions trading, though opposition leaders including Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage sharply criticized the terms and economic projections.
articles.description: The prime minister will tell MPs the deal agreed on Friday is a "choice between a broken status quo or change".

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence market driven by massive infrastructure investments
articles.title: AI reality check: Leadership turmoil, IPO jitters and the fragility of big tech
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence has emerged as a major investment driver on Wall Street, with companies investing heavily in infrastructure to support the evolving technology. Nvidia corporation has become a central semiconductor supplier, while technology giants Microsoft, Amazon and Google have committed substantial funds toward data centre development, alongside artificial intelligence developers OpenAI and Anthropic.
articles.description: As financial markets begin to question the economics, reliability and sustainability of the AI revolution, the AI trade faces its most significant reality check yet

articles.headline: Eastern Libyan commander Khalifa Haftar arrives in Ankara for meetings
articles.title: Libya’s Haftar visits Turkiye days after Ukraine hits Russian warship
articles.summary: Eastern Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar arrived in Ankara on Tuesday for his first known visit to Turkiye, accompanied by his sons Khaled and Belqasim. According to reports, Haftar is set to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The visit follows a Ukrainian attack on a Russian ship in Benghazi that killed ten crew members. The trip also comes as Turkiye builds ties with Haftar's camp alongside its alliance with Tripoli.
articles.description: Ahead of Erdogan’s Libya trip, Haftar’s visit suggests Turkiye seeks another way to bring the country's rivals together.

articles.headline: US Army plans controlled detonation of lead azide in Iowa
articles.title: US Army to detonate more than 4 tonnes of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday
articles.summary: The United States Army announced plans to conduct two consecutive controlled detonations of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Wednesday at 9am. Major General Eric Shirley stated that inaction is no longer an option because the explosive compound becomes unstable in cold weather. Environmental groups and legal challenges previously delayed the blast, which will destroy 68 drums containing roughly 4,500 kilograms of deteriorating material used in munitions since World War I.
articles.description: Despite alarm about toxic lead, federal officials say destroying the unstable explosives is the safest course of action.

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks responses on public interest litigation regarding anti-defection law reforms
articles.title: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 23, 2026, sought responses from the central government, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission regarding a public interest litigation filed by A. Sethu. The petition raises concerns about the alleged misuse of strategic resignations by elected representatives to evade disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.
articles.description: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments

articles.headline: Indian and Nepali prime ministers hold bilateral talks in New Delhi
articles.title: PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah met at Hyderabad House on November 23, 2026, to review relations and expand cooperation in trade, energy, and infrastructure. Accompanied by a 34-member delegation, Mr. Shah also attended a business forum and paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat during his two-day State visit to India, according to official reports.
articles.description: Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, on a two-day State visit, laid a wreath at Raj Ghat and received a Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan before the talks at Hyderabad House

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang denies White House involvement in his return
articles.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
articles.summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang apologized to staff during an all-hands meeting on Tuesday, calling claims that President Donald Trump secured his reinstatement completely untrue. Huang resigned on November twelfth following relationship disclosures, but the board reinstated him on Monday. Huang admitted to violating company policy and stated he is attending daily therapy while facing upcoming congressional questioning on December first.
articles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket's Marisa Kabas. During the meeting, Huang […]

articles.headline: Turkish Air Force helicopter crash kills five crew members in Eskisehir
articles.title: Turkish military helicopter crash kills five in western Turkiye
articles.summary: A Turkish Air Force AS-532 Cougar helicopter crashed near Yorukakcayir village after taking off from Eskisehir for training purposes, killing five crew members. According to the Ministry of National Defence, search and rescue operations continued at the wreckage site located about 15 kilometres west of Eskisehir city centre. The incident occurred twelve days after another military helicopter crash in southern Turkiye killed four personnel near Malatya.
articles.description: The Defence Ministry did not elaborate on the cause of the crash, days after another deadly army helicopter accident.

articles.headline: Saurav Das stopped at Delhi airport following passport office notice
articles.title: Chennai Regional Passport Office notice led to CJP’s Saurav Das being stopped at Delhi airport
articles.summary: Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party, was prevented from boarding a London-bound flight at Delhi airport on November 23, 2026. The action followed a show-cause notice from the Regional Passport Office in Chennai regarding alleged discrepancies in his identity documents. The Madras High Court previously ordered a probe into his nationality status.
articles.description: Saurav Das was served the notice at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before his flight; the government has not issued any statement on the reasons for stopping him at the Delhi airport

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA warns against unlicensed health supplement sales and claims
articles.title: Maharashtra FDA commissioner warns against unlicensed sale of whey protein, misleading health claims
articles.summary: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe issued a strict warning on November 23, 2026, targeting gym operators selling unauthorized health supplements and manufacturers making misleading claims. The move follows a comprehensive compliance order issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act, mandating valid food registrations and prohibiting unverified health claims.
articles.description: FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe urges youngsters to exercise caution while consuming health supplements; gym operators selling such products without authorisation to face action

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit ends without consensus after fossil fuel omissions.
articles.title: How did the COP31 climate agreement fall apart – and what happens now?
articles.summary: The COP31 global climate summit in Turkey concluded without a final agreement after the European Union rejected a draft text that omitted references to phasing out fossil fuels. Major oil producers Saudi Arabia and Russia blocked transition language, exposing deep divisions between developed and developing nations over finance and emissions cuts. Despite the stalled official negotiations, numerous countries and businesses backed alternative electrification and transition pledges outside the formal agenda.
articles.description: In a year of unprecedented climate disasters, a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming, the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment

articles.headline: Alice Huang maintained contact with Chinese intelligence during Nvidia affair
articles.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, says NYT
articles.summary: Alice Huang maintained communication with an intelligence officer from China's Ministry of State Security for over a year during her affair with former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. United States officials continue to investigate Huang and her former company Megaspeed International regarding advanced chip exports. The revelation follows Jensen Huang's resignation and has intensified scrutiny from lawmakers regarding export controls.
articles.description: Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment

articles.headline: India responds strongly against New Zealand with dominant batting performance in Wellington
articles.title: A ‘Pant’astic rewriting of the batting lexicon
articles.summary: India mounted a strong response to New Zealand's 368 runs at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, featuring a 130-run opening partnership between K.L. Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal. Devdutt Padikkal and Rahul added 165 runs for the second wicket before Rahul was dismissed after a long innings. Captain Shubman Gill scored 98 runs, and Rishabh Pant subsequently came to the crease during the third day of the match.

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces launch drone attacks on Russian vessels near Libyan coast
articles.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine was behind drone attacks on Russian ships off Libya
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian forces sank a Russian warship named Merkury and struck a cargo ship named MV Angara using naval drones off the coast of Libya on November 23, 2026. The United Nations Support Mission in Libya expressed serious concern over the incident and called for an immediate independent investigation into the attacks.
articles.description: President Zelenskyy says Ukrainian forces sank the Russian warship Merkury in an "exemplary" sea drone operation.

articles.headline: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes fastest List A double hundred against United Arab Emirates
articles.title: Sooryavanshi smashes fastest List A double hundred
articles.summary: India A batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a world record on Tuesday by scoring the fastest double hundred in List A cricket against the United Arab Emirates during the Rising Stars Asia Cup. The fifteen-year-old left-hander reached the milestone in fifty-two balls and finished with two hundred four runs from fifty-three balls, featuring seven fours and twenty-eight sixes. India A won the match by seven wickets in fourteen point two overs.
articles.description: Sooryavanshi surpassed Jake Fraser-McGurk's record of a 29-ball 100, set in 2023; the third-fastest ton is from South African great AB de Villiers

articles.headline: Xiamen Airlines agrees to purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft
articles.title: China Southern Airlines unit to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 planes
articles.summary: China Southern Airlines announced on Tuesday that its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines signed an agreement to acquire fifty Boeing 737-8 aircraft at a list price of approximately seven point four billion dollars. The planes are scheduled for delivery between 2031 and 2034, subject to shareholder and government approvals, supporting the development of the new Xiamen Xiang'an international airport.
articles.description: The agreement marks the US planemaker's first major order from China in almost a decade.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez secures record-equalling eighth premier-class world championship title
articles.title: MotoGP maestro Marquez makes history with eighth premier-class world title
articles.summary: Ducati rider Marc Marquez secured his eighth premier-class world championship at the Portuguese Grand Prix on November 23, 2026, after finishing eighth in the race won by Marco Bezzecchi. The 33-year-old Spaniard equalled Italian great Giacomo Agostini's historic record following a challenging season that required a remarkable comeback from injuries and surgeries.
articles.description: His eighth success in the premier class of motorcycling pulled Marc Marquez level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini.

articles.headline: House general counsel denies backing federal raid on Ilhan Omar's home
articles.title: US House counsel denies backing controversial raid on Ilhan Omar’s home
articles.summary: Matthew Berry, the United States House of Representatives' top lawyer, rejected claims by federal prosecutors that his office endorsed an October 12 raid on Representative Ilhan Omar's Washington, DC residence. Berry stated the Department of Justice misrepresented his refusal to participate as agreement that constitutional protections did not apply. The investigation involves allegations of immigration fraud against Omar.
articles.description: Legal counsel challenges DOJ's assertion of House's involvement in controversial raid on Ilhan Omar's home.

articles.headline: Emir of Daura suspended following sexual assault allegations by tourist
articles.title: Nigerian monarch, 92, suspended after sexual assault claims
articles.summary: Umar Farouk Umar, the 92-year-old Emir of Daura in northern Nigeria, was suspended from all official engagements and travel after a Polish tourist alleged he grabbed her chest during a November 14 encounter. Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda formed a committee to investigate the claims. The emir has not commented on the allegations or his suspension from the traditional role.
articles.description: The Emir of Daura is one of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, with politicians often trying to gain his support.

articles.headline: Indian Olympic Association prepares for leadership election without P.T. Usha
articles.title: No Usha, Indian Olympic Association set to get a new president
articles.summary: The Indian Olympic Association is set to elect a new president and executive council on December 5, 2026, as incumbent P.T. Usha did not file nominations. Rajeev Mehta, Gagan Narang, and Virender Sachdeva are contesting the top post. The upcoming leadership transition aims to steer the national sports body for the next four years amid active political discussions.
articles.description: Three-way contest expected for the top spot among Gagan Narang, Rajeev Mehta and Virender Sachdeva

articles.headline: Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstates Senegal as Africa Cup champion

articles.headline: Brazilian president Lula da Silva won a historic runoff election after overcoming early adversity.
articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.summary: Born in Pernambuco on October 27, 1945, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva overcame extreme poverty and the loss of a finger in a factory accident to emerge as a prominent trade union leader during Brazil's military dictatorship. After facing decades of political attacks and arrests, he made history on October 25, 2026, by winning the presidential runoff following a second-place finish in the October 4 first round.
articles.description: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

articles.headline: Brazilian President Lula da Silva campaigned across cities ahead of the presidential runoff.
articles.title: Lula takes to streets with people’s demands as Flávio leans on Big Tech in Brazil’s presidential race
articles.summary: Millions of supporters demonstrated across Brazil in mid-October 2026 to demand protections for public services ahead of the presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Capitalizing on widespread street mobilization, the Brazilian Senate approved a bill on October 15, 2026, to reduce the maximum working week to forty hours and guarantee two days of paid rest.
articles.description: In São Paulo, South America’s financial capital, around a million people marched last on October 18 with Workers’ Party banners and placards, demanding protection for public education, healthcare, and transport

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro became the far-right challenger in the Brazilian presidential race.
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro | The Lula challenger
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro entered the presidential race as the far-right challenger following legal difficulties faced by his relatives. His father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a twenty-seven-year sentence for plotting a coup against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Additional family members faced legal troubles or maintained low profiles, leaving Flávio to accidentally assume leadership of the political movement.
articles.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro’s son, running a pro-business campaign backed by evangelical groups, has emerged as a leading figure on Brazil’s far right

articles.headline: Poland confirms second Russian assassination attempt targeting Ukrainian rapper
articles.title: Poland says Russia tried to assassinate Ukrainian rapper twice
articles.summary: Polish and Danish authorities stated that Russian intelligence services targeted Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev, known as Kyivstoner, in two separate assassination plots. Polish officials confirmed an August 2026 plot in Poland and the arrest of a suspect, while Denmark reported a September attempt near Copenhagen, leading to the expulsion of a Russian diplomat. Russia dismissed the allegations as unsubstantiated.
articles.description: Polish confirmation comes after Copenhagen reveals alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen on Danish soil.

articles.summary: World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus appealed for an end to hostilities after clashes in Ituri province disrupted medical operations. Health personnel and relatives were forced to shelter in a maternity ward for over a day. As of November 17, the Democratic Republic of the Congo recorded 5,678 fatalities from 11,613 cases, representing the nation's largest outbreak while ongoing violence complicates relief delivery.

articles.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

articles.headline: Wild indris in Madagascar use opera-like mouth movements to project songs
articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin discovered that wild indri lemurs in Madagascar open their mouths wider when producing higher-pitched calls, mirroring vocal tract tuning used by human opera singers. The study analyzed 83 video recordings of 19 primates, revealing how convergent evolution enables these endangered mammals to project sound across dense rainforests.
articles.description: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

articles.title: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
articles.summary: Asian financial markets experienced sharp declines as investors worried about the long-term viability of the artificial intelligence boom. Japanese markets remained closed for Labour Thanksgiving Day during the trading session.

articles.headline: India AI funding nears 1.6 billion dollars in the first nine months
articles.title: India AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6 billion in nine months of 2026: Tracxn report
articles.summary: Indian artificial intelligence companies raised 1.6 billion dollars in equity funding during the first nine months of 2026, marking a 96 percent increase compared to the previous year, according to a report by Tracxn. Mumbai surpassed Bengaluru as the leading recipient city, driven largely by massive funding rounds secured by enterprises such as Neysa and Sarvam.
articles.description: Mumbai overtook Bengaluru as the largest recipient of AI funding in the country during the period, shows the report, which places India ninth among countries in terms of AI funding raised

articles.summary: A car bomb detonated outside regional government offices in Villavicencio, Colombia, injuring at least 23 people and damaging surrounding buildings. President Abelardo de la Espriella attributed the attack to narcoterrorism amid an ongoing military offensive against armed criminal groups, following earlier explosive incidents involving police and military infrastructure across the country.
articles.description: The explosion is the latest in a string of attacks on buildings housing the security forces and government offices.

articles.headline: Trump criticises Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer amid upcoming leadership vote
articles.title: Trump criticises Schumer amid push for new Democrat leadership in US Senate
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump expressed opposition to Senator Chuck Schumer retaining his position as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress. The debate highlights internal divisions within the Democratic Party following the November midterm elections. A closed-door ballot is scheduled for December 1, while Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is mounting a challenge against the incumbent New York lawmaker.
articles.description: Schumer, who has led the Democrats since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid for majority leader.

articles.headline: Karnataka delegation visits Osaka waste incineration plant to study technology
articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister-led delegation visits Osaka waste-to-energy plant
articles.summary: A delegation led by Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar visited the Maishima waste incineration plant in Osaka on Tuesday to examine Japan’s waste-to-energy model. The facility processes up to 900 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily with a 32-megawatt power generation capacity, as the state seeks long-term solutions for urban waste management.
articles.description: The delegation examined the plant’s technology, which processes up to 900 tonnes of municipal solid waste a day and has a power generation capacity of 32 MW.

articles.headline: Telangana agriculture sector non-performing assets reach ₹7,304 crore
articles.title: Telangana’s agriculture sector NPAs pegged at ₹7,304 crore
articles.summary: Telangana reported agricultural non-performing assets totaling ₹7,304.66 crore as of September 30th, representing 3.65 percent of total outstanding loans. Short-term crop loans accounted for the highest share at ₹4,213 crore across 4.87 lakh accounts. Banks urged the government to expedite pending reimbursements related to interest subvention schemes and cheque printing charges.

articles.headline: Police register FIR over bomb threat targeting singer Diljit Dosanjh concert
articles.title: Bomb threat email targets Diljit Dosanjh’s Bengaluru concert; North Cybercrime Police register FIR
articles.summary: The North Division Cybercrime Police registered an FIR on November 9th following an email threatening an improvised explosive device blast at singer Diljit Dosanjh’s upcoming November 29th concert at NICE Grounds in Bengaluru. The threatening message was sent to the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation commissioner and referenced the slogan Khalistan Zindabad.
articles.description: The email threatened an IED blast during Mr. Dosanjh’s concert as well as at Madavara Metro Station. The email ended with the slogan “Khalistan Zindabad”.

articles.summary: An Iranian singer and four production team members were sentenced to 74 lashes each for publishing obscene content online, according to an Iranian news website on November 23, 2026. articles.headline: Kerala High Court grants bail to Sri Lankan national in LTTE case
articles.title: Kerala HC grants bail to Sri Lankan who was part of ‘transnational conspiracy’ to revive LTTE
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court granted bail to Muhammed Asmin, a Sri Lankan national accused of participating in a transnational conspiracy to revive the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam. articles.headline: Delhi High Court mandates transfer of Juvenile Justice Act cases
articles.title: Delhi High Court says pending cases under Juvenile Justice Act must go to Children’s Courts
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court ruled on November 23, 2026, that all pending cases under the Juvenile Justice Act must be transferred to Children’s Courts. The bench clarified that this procedural change applies retrospectively following a 2022 amendment. However, the court noted that general criminal offences involving minors do not require transfer to these specialized courts.
articles.description: A Bench of Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Arun Bhardwaj passed the ruling on November 23 while answering two legal questions referred to it by an Additional Sessions Judge at Saket Courts

articles.headline: Student injured following accidental firearm discharge at Palakkad school
articles.title: Class 9 student injured after gun goes off at school in Keralam
articles.summary: A ninth-grade student sustained non-serious injuries after a country-made gun discharged at a government school near Thrithala on November 24, 2026. According to local law enforcement, another pupil allegedly brought the weapon onto the campus. Medical personnel treated the victim at a hospital while authorities continue investigating how the firearm entered the facility and the precise circumstances surrounding the unexpected incident.

articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir declared on November 24, 2026, that deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina can only enter Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance. articles.description: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

articles.headline: Herat residents stage rare protests against Taliban regime restrictions
articles.title: How Herat defied the Taliban regime, chanting ‘women, work and freedom’
articles.summary: Residents in Herat staged a rare public demonstration in mid-June chanting slogans for women, work, and freedom. Taliban officials subsequently announced arrests for women violating the Islamic dress code, initiating a strict crackdown across the city.
articles.description: The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested

articles.summary: Mexican military forces detained high-profile drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa state following an operation that resulted in eleven deaths, including four soldiers. articles.description: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.

articles.headline: Nine people killed in three separate road accidents across Andhra Pradesh districts
articles.title: Nine killed in three road accidents in Andhra, five of them near Bhogapuram
articles.summary: Nine people died in three separate road accidents across Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, and Palnadu districts in Andhra Pradesh. Five individuals died when their SUV rammed into a stationary lorry near Bhogapuram. Two tipper lorry occupants died in a fire after a collision in Anakapalli, and two Ayyappa devotees died when their car fell into a canal in Palnadu district.
articles.description: Seven of the nine were pilgrims heading home: five from the Srimukhalingam temple, whose SUV hit a parked lorry near Bhogapuram and two Ayyappa devotees returning from Amaravati

articles.headline: Union Home Minister Amit Shah says Kartarpur Corridor will reopen after security resolution
articles.title: Kartarpur Corridor will be reopened as soon as national security concerns are resolved, says Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated that the Kartarpur Corridor will reopen as soon as national security concerns are resolved. Speaking in Delhi, Shah criticized Congress for the historical division and noted the corridor was closed following Operation Sindoor in May 2025. Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh had earlier sent a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging the corridor's reopening.
articles.description: “It was solely due to the carelessness of the Congress that such a sacred, major site is not a part of India today,” Amit Shah said

articles.headline: Karnataka chief minister urges protesting ASHA workers to end agitation
articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister speaks to protesting ASHA workers from Japan, urges them to call off stir
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar appealed on November 24, 2026, to protesting ASHA workers in Bengaluru to withdraw their indefinite agitation. articles.description: The call came amid criticism from the protesters over Mr. Shivakumar’s Japan visit while their agitation was under way. A song parodying his foreign trip and questioning his response to their demands has also gone viral on social media.

articles.description: The sixth Earthshot Prize, founded by Britain’s Prince William to promote innovative climate change solutions, will be presented in Mumbai on November 17, 2026

articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India has granted permission for a lamp to be lit on the Thirupparankundram Hill for the Karthigai Deepam festival on November 24, 2026. articles.description: The Pakistan Air Force pilot will spend about a week on board the Tiangong, conducting experiments with China’s crew.

articles.headline: History of world chess championships and legendary players examined
articles.title: World chess championship: Genuises who wielded their magic
articles.summary: Emanuel Lasker held the record as the longest-reigning world chess champion for twenty-seven years, beginning in 1894 when he defeated Wilhelm Steinitz in New York, Philadelphia, and Montreal. articles.headline: D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov prepare for World chess championship in Geneva
articles.title: World chess championship: A fascinating duel between two brilliant young minds

articles.description: Gukesh has to reproduce the kind of chess that made him a force in the couple of years leading up to the last Worlds; Sindarov has been almost unstoppable of late; it will be the youngest title showdown in the history of the tournament
